'''Frank Rawle Haig''', [[Society of Jesus|S.J.]] (September 11, 1928 – February 28, 2024) was an American [[Jesuit]] priest, physicist and academic administrator. He served as the third [[College president|President]] of [[Wheeling Jesuit University]] from 1966 to 1972 and the seventh president of [[Le Moyne College]] from 1981 until 1987.

==Biography==

===Early life===
Born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], on September 11, 1928,<ref name="google">{{cite book|title=American Men & Women of Science|author=R.R. Bowker Company. Database Publishing Group|date=2009|volume=3|publisher=Thomson/Gale|isbn=9781414433035|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lldYAAAAMAAJ|access-date=2015-03-22}}</ref> Haig was the younger brother of [[Alexander Haig]], who served as the [[United States Secretary of State]] under [[Ronald Reagan]] from 1981 until 1982. Haig entered the Jesuit order in [[Wernersville, Pennsylvania]] shortly after graduating from Lower Merion Senior High School in [[Lower Merion Township, Pennsylvania]] in 1946. Thereafter, he received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from [[Woodstock College]] in 1952, a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in philosophy from Bellarmine College in [[Plattsburgh, New York]] in 1953 and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[theoretical physics]] from the [[Catholic University of America]] in 1959. He also earned a second licentiate in sacred theology from Woodstock College in 1961, the year of his ordination.<ref name=wju>{{cite news|title=Wheeling Jesuit University 1960's: Third President - Father Frank R. Haig, S.J., 1966-72|url=http://www.wju.edu/about/history/1960s.asp|work=[[Wheeling Jesuit University]]|access-date=2010-02-25|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528175300/http://www.wju.edu/about/history/1960s.asp|archive-date=2010-05-28}}</ref>

===Wheeling College, Johns Hopkins University, and Loyola University Maryland===
Haig joined the faculty of the [[physics]] department at [[Wheeling College]], which is now known as Wheeling University and no longer affiliated with the Jesuits, in 1963 after completing a [[postdoctoral fellowship]] at the [[University of Rochester]].<ref name=wju/>

Haig was appointed the third president of Wheeling College in 1966, succeeded the school's second head, Father [[William F. Troy]], S.J.<ref name=wju/> Haig was [[inaugurated]] president on July 15, 1966.<ref name=wju/> In his acceptance speech, Haig told the audience, "The world will be what our men and women of insight make it to be...It is a challenge to be asked to help them see all right."<ref name=wju/>

Haig remained president until his resignation on August 21, 1972. He was succeeded by [[Charles Currie Jr.]], S.J. While serving as a visiting fellow at [[Johns Hopkins University]], Haig became in 1972 an [[astrophysics]] professor with the department of physics, engineering and computer science at [[Loyola University Maryland]] (also in [[Baltimore, Maryland]]),<ref name="rblmd240301f">[https://www.loyola.edu/news/2024/0301-loyola-celebrates-life-of-jesuit-frank-haig.html Buettner, Rita. "Loyola celebrates the life of the Rev. Frank Haig, S.J., professor emeritus of physics," Loyola University Maryland, Friday, March 1, 2024.] Retrieved March 1, 2024.</ref> where he served as chair during the 1980–1981 academic year.<ref name=wju/>

===Le Moyne College===
Haig was appointed the president of [[Le Moyne College]] in [[Syracuse, New York]], in 1981, succeeding Father [[William J. O'Halloran]], S.J.

Haig became acting president of Le Moyne College on January 1, 1981.<ref name=nyt>{{cite news|first=Albin|last=Krebs|title=NOTES ON PEOPLE; A Haig Inaugurated |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1982/01/25/nyregion/notes-on-people-a-haig-inaugurated.html |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=1982-01-25 |access-date=2010-02-25}}</ref> He was formally inaugurated as the college's seventh president on Friday, January 22, 1982.<ref name=nyt/>

Haig remained president of Le Moyne until 1987 and was succeeded by [[Acting (law)|interim]] president [[James C. Finlay]], S.J.

===Later life===
Haig returned to Loyola in 1987 and was named [[professor emeritus]] of physics in 2005.<ref name="rblmd240301f"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Frank Haig - Faculty - Loyola University Maryland|url=https://www.loyola.edu/about/community/faculty/haig|access-date=2021-02-26|website=www.loyola.edu}}</ref> He received the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Washington Academy of Sciences at its annual meeting in Washington, D.C., on May 19, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rev. Frank Haig, S.J., receives lifetime achievement award from Washington Academy of Sciences - Newsroom - Loyola University Maryland|url=https://www.loyola.edu/about/community/faculty/~/link.aspx?_id=D025BC2E074046ADA5D8BB2D43BDAD0A&_z=z|access-date=2021-02-26|website=www.loyola.edu}}</ref>  He served on the Scientific and Educational Council of the Maryland Academy of Science and as treasurer of the Washington Academy of Sciences. He presented papers and lectures both in the United States and abroad and lived at the Manresa Hall Jesuit Community on the campus of [[St. Joseph's University]] in Philadelphia until his death.

Haig died in [[Merion, Pennsylvania]], on February 28, 2024, at the age of 95.<ref name="rblmd240301f"/>
